summary:
OBSIDIAN Navigator is a cross-platform mobile application, compatible with Android and iOS, developed to visualize, explore, and analyze the surface of Mars, with a special focus on Jezero Crater. It uses NASA topographic data, satellite imagery, and digital elevation models in 2D and 3D, including data related to the robotic missions and rovers that have explored the planet, such as Perseverance and the Ingenuity helicopter.

The application addresses the challenge through an interactive map with cartographic layers, identification of scientific points of interest, and preliminary route planning between two locations (A and B). It also allows users to calculate distances, visualize 2D and 3D topographic profiles, interact with rovers, identify safe and accessible areas, detect steep slopes, and export results.

Its importance lies in transforming NASA scientific data into an accessible technological tool that facilitates virtual exploration using a smart mobile device, terrain analysis, and decision-making for future space exploration missions. It also brings explorers, science, engineering, and technological innovation closer to the study and exploration of Mars.
details:
WHAT EXACTLY DOES IT DO?

OBSIDIAN Navigator is a mobile application for iOS and Android operating systems that allows users to visualize the surface of Mars in 2D and 3D, explore Jezero Crater, and plan preliminary travel routes using NASA topographic data, satellite imagery, and digital elevation models.

Features: What does it allow users to do?

  • Visualize Mars: View the surface of Mars through an interactive 2D and 3D map.
  • Explore Jezero: Zoom in, explore, and navigate Jezero Crater and its different layers.
  • Map Layers: Enable and disable cartographic layers, including satellite imagery, terrain, and other geographic information.
  • Points of Interest: Identify scientific points of interest on the map.
  • Origin and Destination: Select a starting point (A) and a destination point (B).
  • Preliminary Route Planning: Generate a preliminary route between the two selected locations.
  • Distance and Elevation Profile: View the route distance and its topographic elevation profile.
  • Rovers: Interact with the 3D rover model.
  • Steep Slopes: Identify sections of the route with steep slopes.
  • Terrain Information: Access basic information about the Martian terrain.
  • Export Results: Export route-planning results for further consultation and analysis.
  • Planned Additional Feature: An artificial intelligence assistant integrated into the application to answer questions about the terrain and planned routes.

WHAT ARE ITS BENEFITS?

1. TECHNOLOGICAL BENEFIT

Promotes technological innovation through a mobile application that integrates interactive 2D and 3D maps of Mars, satellite imagery, digital elevation models, and artificial intelligence. These features allow users to analyze terrain, visualize 3D rover models, and plan preliminary routes across Jezero Crater.

2. SOCIAL BENEFIT

Promotes education, scientific research, and access to knowledge about Mars by providing students, researchers, and future explorers with an interactive educational tool based on official NASA scientific data. It encourages interest in science, technology, and planetary exploration.

3. ECONOMIC BENEFIT

Helps optimize financial resources and reduce preliminary research and planning costs by freely integrating NASA's publicly available scientific data into a single application. This facilitates terrain analysis and route assessment without relying exclusively on expensive specialized tools.

WHAT DO YOU HOPE TO ACHIEVE?

We aim to make OBSIDIAN Navigator an accessible mobile application for a wider audience, including students and future researchers, through an interactive 2D and 3D platform that allows users to interact with real and reliable scientific information. Our goal is to facilitate knowledge, exploration, and analysis of the Martian surface using NASA scientific data and artificial intelligence integrated through software development.

We seek to contribute to future research and human exploration missions to Mars, bringing space science and technology closer to new generations around the world.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

  • Google AI Studio (Gemini): Generated the base of the web app (React + Vite) and its structure, using the Gemini API template. (aistudio.google.com)
    • Interactive 2D map of Jezero Crater with NASA layers (MOLA, HRSC, THEMIS, Viking, MOC, HiRISE, CTX)
    • 3D terrain model built from MOLA elevation data
    • Slope analysis and hazard levels for route planning
    • Rover simulation (Perseverance and Curiosity): speed, energy and slippage
    • Export of route reports (GeoJSON, GPX, KML, CSV, PNG, PDF)
  • ChatGPT: Initial analysis of the Martian terrain, text writing, and translations. (chatgpt.com)
  • Claude: Code generation and review for the data analysis, and organizing the data sources used by the app. (claude.ai)
  • Grok: Code reviews, error resolution, and quick answers about the project’s technical details. (grok.com)

Development tools

  • Cursor: AI-powered code editor used to edit, test and refine the app’s code. (cursor.com)
  • Visual Studio Code: Code editor used to organize the project files and run the app locally. (code.visualstudio.com)
  • Python: Programming language used for scripts that process and analyze Mars data, such as elevation and slope calculations. (python.org)

Deployment and hosting platforms

  • Vercel: Hosting and deployment of the web app, with automatic builds from the repository. (vercel.com)
  • GitHub Pages: Publishing from the repository, through the workflow found in the app’s code. (pages.github.com)
